rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all align to abdominal aortic aneurysm), so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity plus PRS-comparable performance evidence and study archetype. PGS000753 is preferred because it is disease-focused (Million Veteran Program AAA paper), uses a clean prevalent AAA endpoint with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and—critically—reports a PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), which is a directly PRS-comparable signal per the provided domain guidance. The main limitation is that it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R², while some alternatives report full-model discrimination or PRS-comparable R²/partial-r; however, those metrics are either explicitly covariates-regressed-out but small (e.g., PGS001784 R²≈0.0147; PGS002054 partial-r≈0.0144) or are full-model AUROC/C-index (PGS003972/PGS003973/PGS003429) that cannot be treated as PRS-only and may be covariate-driven. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS003973 and PGS003972 come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) with broad multi-cohort development but only full-model metrics and unknown/limited covariate transparency; PGS002054 and PGS001784 are framework/portability-style scores with explicit PRS-comparable metrics but carry a framework penalty and do not clearly outperform the disease-focused options on PRS-isolated evidence. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target trait alcohol dependence via trait_efo/phenotyping (PGS002738/PGS002739 explicitly map to trait_efo=alcohol dependence with phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder; PGS000201/PGS000202 map to trait_efo=alcohol dependence measurement with phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder DSM-5 criteria count). PGS002738 is best supported because it has the most directly aligned trait_efo (alcohol dependence), a straightforward AUD endpoint, and the strongest visible discriminative evidence among the pool (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96 with CI 1.54–2.51) with a reasonably large EUR evaluation sample (n=7,900) and multi-cohort development (MVP, UKB). Runners-up: PGS000201 next due to the highest reported incremental ΔR² (0.01192) among the DSM-5-count scores and large genome-wide PRS-CS variant count (~1.09M) with EUR evaluation (n=7,599); PGS002739 follows as a direct AUD/alcohol dependence model with supportive OR evidence (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76, CI 1.32–2.34) but evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean ancestry (transportability depends on intended deployment ancestry, which is not provided); PGS000202 is last due to weaker incremental ΔR² (0.00456) and smaller validation (n=1,251) despite similar endpoint/method to PGS000201. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUC/R²) are largely absent across candidates and covariates are unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739, limiting comparability and certainty despite good endpoint alignment.

All 3 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with broadly aligned reported/phenotyped endpoints. PGS004913 is best supported because it is explicitly disease-focused on alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers, with phenotype_reported matching the target closely and PRS-comparable performance reported as R²=0.029 (rather than only a covariate-inflated full-model AUROC), plus a substantial OR (top vs bottom deciles OR=4.4). Main limitation: the reported R² is modest and the training/validation sample sizes are relatively small, so external robustness is uncertain from the visible metadata.

Runners-up: PGS001777 is also disease-focused and reports strong stratification (top 20% vs bottom 20% OR=6.18) but is a very sparse 3-variant score with unknown covariates and small validation (n=1,390), lowering confidence in generalizability. PGS000704 has very large UKB-based development/validation and a modern multi-PRS snpnet approach with many variants, but its only visible discrimination is a full-model C-index/AUC=0.711 (no PGS-only/PRS-comparable metric), so the apparent performance may be largely covariate-driven and is not directly comparable for PRS ranking.

All 19 visible candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping_reported aligns via Angina / I20 ICD10 / PheCode 411.3). The strongest-supported choice from the visible evidence is PGS001262 because it provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.58683; PGS-only R2=0.01304) plus incremental AUROC (0.0098) and uses only basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs) with a direct doctor-diagnosed angina endpoint; its PRS-only R2 is also below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.009–0.014; liability h2≈0.134), avoiding obvious metric implausibility. Runners-up: PGS001261 (time-to-event angina pectoris; similar PRS-only metrics with slightly lower endpoint generality penalty but strong full-model AUROC), PGS001260 (similar framework/snpnet sibling with slightly weaker metrics), then among the MVP PheCode models the best-supported are those with the strongest per-SD effect sizes and strong full-model C-index (PGS005048 OR=1.487; PGS005052 OR=1.491), though these lack clear PRS-only metrics and have N/A training sample details in the visible metadata. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY) because the top candidates are dominated by pan-trait UKB framework scores (the '813 traits' paper) which domain guidance flags as often less reliable externally, while the more recent ICD10/PheCode alternatives largely lack PRS-only performance metrics, leaving residual uncertainty despite direct phenotype alignment. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align to ankylosing spondylitis), so a direct-match exists. Among the EUR-evaluated options, PGS002089 (LDpred2; 22,026 variants; UKB-derived) is structurally the strongest genome-wide shrinkage model and has the highest reported PRS-comparable metric available in this pool (partial correlation 0.0919, EUR validation). Runners-up: PGS001267 and PGS001268 report explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² and incremental AUROC, but they come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits") with only 10 variants, which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk; between them, the non–time-to-event endpoint (PGS001267) is slightly cleaner for a generic disease target. PGS001876 is another EUR portability-framework score with weaker partial correlation (0.0797) and fewer variants than PGS002089. PGS003420 is a disease-focused EAS-only study with a relatively high reported full-model AUROC (0.7886), but lacks PRS-only metrics and is ancestry-restricted, limiting comparability versus the EUR-evaluated models. Overall confidence is moderate (not high) because the strongest structural candidate (PGS002089) comes from a portability/framework context and key PRS-only AUC/R² metrics are missing for several competitors, making cross-candidate performance comparability incomplete. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254) plus closely aligned aortic valve function measures mapped to aortic stenosis (PGS005255/PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is an exact trait match (trait_reported/trait_efo = aortic stenosis) with endpoint-fidelity phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis cases), a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with large variant count (~1.12M), and it reports a strong time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) alongside a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92). Main limitation: the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariate adjustment (multiple cardiometabolic comorbidities and risk factors), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be isolated from the visible metadata.

Runner-up ordering: PGS005254 is the next-best exact aortic stenosis model (PRS-CS, ~1.11M variants) with a strong HR (1.64, with CI) and comparatively lighter covariates (age/sex/PCs), but lacks any AUC/C-index/R². PGS005255 and PGS005256 are slightly less direct because their trait_reported are valve-function measurements (mean pressure gradient; peak aortic velocity) even though trait_efo includes aortic stenosis and phenotyping_reported is incident aortic stenosis; they have moderate HRs (~1.53) and similarly light covariates but no discrimination metrics. As a distant remaining option from the visible list, PGS004911 is not a direct match (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), included only because the candidate list contains no additional aortic-stenosis-aligned models beyond the four above.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including exact EFO matches: PGS001135 ("Arthritis (nos)", trait_efo=arthritis) and the "Other arthritis" models PGS004477/PGS004547 (trait_efo=arthritis). PGS001135 is selected as best because it has the most explicit, PRS-comparable performance evidence among the arthritis-EFO models (reports PGS-only AUROC=0.53928 and PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291, plus incremental AUROC=0.00314), enabling a clearer assessment of standalone PRS contribution than the alternatives, which mainly report only an OR without PRS-only metrics. However, overall quality remains sub-optimal because PGS001135 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework study ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable in external validation than disease-focused scores, and its PRS-only metrics are modest. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS004547 and PGS004477 are exact arthritis-EFO but provide limited comparable performance (single OR only, unknown covariates), and PGS000114 (juvenile idiopathic arthritis) and PGS001290 (osteoarthritis) are direct arthritis-spectrum endpoints with clearer disease specificity but are not exact generic-arthritis endpoints for the broad target.

All listed candidates are direct matches to asthma (trait_efo=asthma or closely aligned childhood/pediatric asthma). PGS002727 is best supported because it is explicitly disease-focused for pediatric asthma, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.57) and a reasonable full-model AUROC (0.66), and has very large validation support (n=391,820), with multi-ancestry evaluation indicated. Key limitation: covariates are listed as Unknown and the endpoint is pediatric asthma (not generic all-ages asthma), so comparability to general asthma risk is not fully resolved from the visible metadata.

Runners-up: PGS001782 (PRS-CS-auto; asthma; AUROC 0.659 plus covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.048844; multi-biobank training; EUR eval) and PGS001787 (PRS-CS-auto; asthma; AUROC 0.64; R2=0.035168; very large validation n=351,578) have strong, PRS-comparable R2 evidence but come from a global-biobank framework-style paper (penalized per domain guidance vs disease-focused). PGS001344 (snpnet; doctor-diagnosed asthma) has the strongest full-model AUROC among the UKB sparse-framework siblings shown (0.666) with reported PGS-only AUROC/R2, but is still from the pan-trait UKB framework family. PGS002061 (LDpred2; asthma) is a strong method and shows the best partial-r among the UKB portability paper siblings (0.1184), but lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 and is from a portability framework, limiting certainty. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo includes atopic eczema). The best-supported direct-match for generic atopic eczema risk is PGS002755 because its phenotyping_reported is a general, endpoint-faithful definition (“Incident atopic dermatitis”) rather than a therapy-induced/paradoxical eczema phenotype, and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,090,702), which is structurally favorable for a polygenic disease. Its reported effect size is modest but usable (HR high vs low PRS 1.249, EUR eval). Main limitation: no PRS-only AUROC/R² is reported, so comparative performance is hard to judge and confidence cannot be high.

Runners-up: PGS004587 is also endpoint-faithful (“Incident atopic dermatitis”) but is a sparse 23-SNP GWAS-hits score with similarly modest HR (1.153), making it structurally weaker than PRS-CS. PGS001773 targets a narrower subtype (“Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis”) and reports a very high full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49) with demographic/ethnicity covariates, but domain guidance warns not to treat full-model AUROC/R² as PRS-comparable; the magnitude also raises concern it is largely covariate-driven and/or non-comparable to PRS-only metrics. The remaining three (PGS003486, PGS003459, PGS004903) are primarily evaluated on “paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis” (therapy-induced/restricted endpoint), which is a weaker match to generic atopic eczema; among them, PGS003486 and PGS003459 have small AUROC (~0.57–0.59) and modest ORs, and PGS004903 has unclear covariates and reports only a coefficient/p-value, so they rank below the incident-atopic-dermatitis models.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (atrial fibrillation) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. PGS005168 is best supported because it comes from a disease-focused AF meta-analysis (Nat Genet; multi-cohort development listed), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), and reports strong discrimination in the selected European validation record (C-index 0.8718 with CI) plus a per-SD HR ~1.67. Key limitation: the reported C-index appears to be a full-model metric (covariates include CHARGE-AF), and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the magnitude is not directly comparable across models and may be covariate-influenced.

Runners-up: (1) PGS002814 is also disease-focused (Nat Genet cross-ancestry AF GWAS), very large training sample, and reports strong effect size (OR ~1.94) with AUROC 0.74, but it is evaluated in East Asian only, reducing generality vs the EUR-evaluated best pick. (2) PGS005313 (Nat Commun; PRS-CSx) is disease-focused and reports strong OR ~1.82 with AUROC 0.78, but evaluation is MAE-only, again limiting comparability/portability for generic use. (3) PGS000016 (Nat Genet 2019; LDpred) has explicit PRS-only R2=0.029 (sanity-consistent with the provided AF h2_obs ceiling) and large validation n, but it is an older single-biobank development (UKB) and its headline AUROC is full-model. (4) PGS000331 (Nat Med 2020; LDpred) is disease-relevant with multi-cohort development and HR ~1.62, but has smaller training n and only full-model C-index reported, making it less directly supported than the above. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches to the target trait concept (atrial flutter appears either as the sole endpoint or explicitly within a combined AF/flutter endpoint). PGS001263 is preferred because it is the only exact atrial-flutter-specific model (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Atrial flutter”) and it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.61716; PGS-only R2=0.02517) with basic covariates; its PRS-only R2 is also below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), so nothing is obviously inconsistent. However, confidence is limited because the best-supported alternatives are for the combined endpoint “atrial fibrillation and flutter” (PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050), and two of those (PGS001841, PGS002050) come from a portability framework paper and lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only partial-r), making cross-model performance comparison incomplete; additionally, PGS001339 is time-to-event, which is a mild endpoint mismatch versus generic disease status. Runner-up ordering reflects remaining direct-match support: PGS001339 retains strong concept alignment and has PRS-only metrics (though for combined AF/flutter and TTE), while PGS002050 and PGS001841 have weaker comparability due to missing PRS-only AUROC/R2 despite larger training and more modern genome-wide methods.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to autism spectrum disorder). PGS000327 is best supported because its endpoint fidelity is coherent across fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder”), it comes from an ASD-focused publication (“Identification of common genetic risk variants for autism spectrum disorder.”), and it provides supportive PRS-relevant evidence including an OR=1.33 (moderate per-SD effect) plus a reported R² metric (full_model_r2=0.0245) in European validation. By contrast, PGS002790 has an explicit endpoint mismatch in phenotyping_reported (“Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”) despite trait_reported being ASD, and its reported metric is a small partial R² (~0.00546) with no effect sizes shown, making it less directly anchored to ASD diagnosis. Main limitation: neither candidate reports clearly PRS-only (no-covariates) AUC/R², and the available R² fields appear to be full-model/partial metrics, so the strength of PRS-only discrimination is uncertain; this keeps confidence at Moderate.

All 20 visible candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = basal cell carcinoma). The strongest support is for PGS000452 because it has high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported = Basal cell carcinoma), basic covariates only (age/sex/batch/PCs), and the strongest visible performance/effect evidence among the MGI PRSweb sibling set: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647), Nagelkerke R² 0.0487, and a strong per-SD OR 1.663 (1.57–1.761) plus top-1% vs rest OR 3.61. Close runners-up from the same coherent disease-focused PRSweb family include PGS000454 (very similar AUROC 0.632 and R² 0.0489 with comparable covariates), PGS000456 (AUROC 0.63, R² 0.0456, strong top-1% OR 3.95), and PGS000458 (AUROC 0.628, R² 0.0457, top-1% OR 4.03). PGS000457 is the best-supported UKB-trained sibling (endpoint still BCC; basic covariates; AUROC 0.617, R² 0.0322, OR 1.535) and is ranked above other UKB siblings due to slightly stronger metrics. Confidence is not High because many PRSweb siblings are near-ties with small metric differences (domain guidance: small AUROC gaps are often noise), and most reported AUROCs are full-model rather than explicitly PRS-only, limiting strict comparability. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. PGS001824 is preferred because it has the most endpoint-faithful labeling for the target (trait_efo exactly “bilirubin metabolism disease”; phenotyping_reported “Disorders of bilirubin excretion”) and provides a PRS-comparable performance metric (partial correlation 0.0716 with CI) under basic covariates, avoiding reliance on full-model AUROC. PGS002032 is a very close runner-up with the same endpoint, covariates, training/validation context, and identical partial-r, but differs mainly by method/structure (LDpred2 with many variants vs penalized regression with 22 variants); with no additional comparable metrics shown, the evidence is insufficient to clearly separate them, lowering confidence. PGS000924 is a broader composite endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism” time-to-event) from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (snpnet, 5 variants), which domain guidance flags as less reliable for external generalization despite its high reported AUROC/R2; additionally, its PGS-only R2 (0.218) exceeds the provided local h2_obs (~0.089), suggesting non-comparability/scale mismatch and further limiting its support. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present (3 models) with trait_reported/trait_efo aligned to bipolar disorder and its I/II subtypes. However, all three appear to come from the same publication family, use the same method (SDPR), have similar EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, and lack PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (AUC and PRS-only R2 are null; only small partial R² values are shown, and the reported phenotyping_reported fields are not explicit bipolar diagnosis endpoints). With limited and somewhat endpoint-misaligned performance evidence, no candidate is clearly best supported; PGS002786 is selected only because it is the closest concept match to the target trait label (bipolar disorder vs bipolar I/II), while PGS002787 and PGS002788 remain essentially indistinguishable runners-up aside from subtype labeling and similarly small partial R². | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present (3 total), but they map to two different coagulation-related endpoints and all come from pan-trait/portability framework publications rather than a clearly disease-focused coagulation study family, limiting certainty.

Best pick: PGS001033 is the only candidate whose mapped trait_efo exactly matches the target (“blood coagulation disease”) and it provides the richest directly comparable performance metadata (includes PGS-only AUROC 0.634 and PGS-only R² 0.0578, plus full-model AUROC with only basic covariates). However, its endpoint is time-to-event (“TTE other coagulation defects”) and it is an extremely sparse 1-variant snpnet score from the ‘813 traits in UK Biobank’ framework paper—both are warning signals for generalizability.

Runners-up: PGS002034 and PGS001826 target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO (not the broad target), but have coherent phenotype labeling and come from the same portability framework paper with similar partial-r (~0.056). Between them, PGS002034 is structurally preferred due to much larger variant count (LDpred2, 32,552 variants) versus PGS001826 (penalized regression, 45 variants), with essentially identical reported partial-r; remaining ordering is weak due to missing AUROC/R² and the narrower congenital endpoint. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are abundant in the visible list. The strongest-supported cluster is the 2023 Am J Hum Genet “Evaluation of polygenic scoring methods in five biobanks…” family (PGS003983/003999/004025/004040/004053/004069/004083/004107/004123/004137/004153), which is endpoint-aligned (phenotyping_reported: “Breast cancer”), uses no non-genetic covariates (covariates: “0”), and provides comparable discrimination evidence (AUROC with CIs, plus R² and per-SD OR/Beta). Within this coherent family, PGS004153 is best supported because it has the highest reported AUROC (0.6625) and strong accompanying R² (0.0764) and OR (1.826) in the same evaluation context (European; EVAL includes EUR/SAS). Runners-up are selected from the same high-support family based on the next-best AUROC/R²/effect-size package: PGS004040 (AUROC 0.6598; R² 0.0739; OR 1.809), PGS004025 (AUROC 0.6598; R² 0.0736; OR 1.806), PGS004083 (AUROC 0.6553; R² 0.0697; OR 1.775), and PGS004069 (AUROC 0.6558; R² 0.0709; OR 1.784). Confidence is Moderate because many other direct-match models exist (including other large, modern PRS-CS/LDpred-style breast cancer scores), but the visible evidence most consistently favors this internally coherent, endpoint-faithful, PRS-comparable-metrics cluster, with PGS004153 leading by a modest margin.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=celiac disease), with generally good endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is celiac/coeliac disease, except some composites/restricted endpoints). PGS000316 is best supported overall because it targets the generic disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease) and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.879 with CI) with very large validation sample size (n=379,767), providing comparatively robust visible performance evidence among the disease-endpoint-faithful options. Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates listed as Unknown, so the PRS-only contribution cannot be isolated from the visible metadata, lowering certainty versus a model with explicit PRS-only metrics.

Runners-up: PGS001301 has explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.82867; PGS R2(no covariates)=0.14224) and clear covariates, but comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper and uses a broader composite phenotype (Malabsorption/coeliac disease), which domain guidance flags as typically less reliable than disease-focused models. PGS000040 reports very high AUROC=0.9 but only as a full-model metric with unknown covariates and smaller validation (n=2,476), making comparability uncertain. PGS000042 and PGS000041 are restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (endpoint restriction) with moderate full-model AUROC (~0.73), making them less general for generic celiac disease risk despite direct mapping. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported consistently cervical cancer, mostly incident cervical cancer). PGS003428 is best supported on structural and study-focus grounds: it is a disease-focused cervical-phenotypes GWAS meta-analysis paper using a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant count (2,894,555) and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (HR=1.33) with basic covariates (age, smoking) and EUR evaluation. Remaining limitation: it reports only full-model discrimination (C-index=0.613) without PRS-only AUROC/R², and its reported discrimination is not clearly superior to others; thus the overall direct-match evidence is not strong enough for a high-confidence pick.

Runners-up: PGS000073 and PGS000784 are coherent near-clones (10 GWAS-significant variants; same endpoint/covariates; similar HR~1.21–1.22) with large EUR validation (n=211,795), but they come from cross-/pan-cancer risk-factor integration contexts and only provide full-model AUROC/C-index (0.745/0.75) that is discounted as PRS-only evidence. PGS005165 is a direct-match EAS-specific score (15 known loci) with moderate HR=1.2 and EAS evaluation, but ancestry specificity limits general direct-match preference absent a deployment ancestry. PGS003389 (lassosum, 2,814 variants) has weaker reported discrimination (AUROC=0.563) and minimal R² (0.00158), making it the least supported among the non-framework disease-endpoint candidates. PGS001299 is deprioritized because it is a pan-trait UKB framework sparse model (snpnet; 24 variants) with weak PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC~0.55; PGS R²~0.0026), despite having explicit PRS-only reporting.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (either exact cholelithiasis/K80 or a closely related composite endpoint including cholecystitis). The strongest visible PRS-comparable performance evidence among the non-framework, endpoint-faithful options is for the UKB portability siblings: PGS002072 (LDpred2) reports the highest partial correlation (partial-r=0.098, EUR validation) versus PGS001861 (penalized regression; partial-r=0.0948), with otherwise identical endpoint/covariates/publication context, making PGS002072 the best-supported pick within that coherent family. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS001861 is the near-twin with slightly lower partial-r; PGS004546 and PGS004476 are exact K80 cholelithiasis models but provide only modest effect-size evidence (OR~1.30 and ~1.22, respectively) and have unknown covariates, limiting comparability; PGS001174 is an exact cholelithiasis time-to-event model with explicit PRS-only metrics, but it comes from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused alternatives, so it is deprioritized despite having more complete AUC/R2 reporting. Overall confidence is moderate because key metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) are missing for most candidates and the available metrics are not fully comparable across study archetypes/endpoints (composite vs K80 vs TTE). | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = chronic kidney disease), so ranking is driven by endpoint fidelity plus the most PRS-informative performance evidence available (prefer PRS-only metrics or per-SD OR/HR), while discounting covariate-heavy full-model AUROC. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD-focused (Nat Med: “Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”), uses a clinically specific CKD definition (stage 3+ / eGFR<45), has large development (n=279,819), multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.47) alongside a high reported AUROC (0.78) in European validation. Main limitation: the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric with many clinical covariates, and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-only contribution cannot be cleanly compared across models.

Runners-up: PGS005090 is CKD stage 3+ with very strong reported discrimination (AUROC=0.9, R²=0.1) and a solid OR (1.41) in African American evaluation, but comparability is limited by ancestry specificity (AFR-only GWAS/EVAL) and lack of PRS-only metrics clarity. PGS005113 has a strong OR (1.35) with clean/basic covariates and CKDGen training context, but lacks explicit AUROC/R². PGS004889 targets incident CKD without diabetes and reports HR=1.3 with multi-ancestry evaluation, but the endpoint is more restricted (incident, non-diabetic) and uses a bundled clinical risk score covariate, reducing PRS comparability. PGS002757 is a generic CKD PRS-CS score with modest OR (1.15) and limited supporting metrics, but retains direct phenotype alignment.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). PGS001783 is best supported overall because it is an exact COPD endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both COPD) and, among the direct COPD-labeled options, it provides comparatively strong PRS-comparable evidence via a covariates-regressed-out/Nagelkerke R2 (0.038092) plus a reported AUROC (0.74) in the selected European validation record; its PRS-only R2 is also consistent with the provided COPD heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0388), passing the sanity-check. Main limitation: it comes from a global biobank framework-style paper (not a single disease-focused consortium) and lacks a clearly labeled PGS-only AUROC, so the AUROC may not be directly comparable across candidates.

Runners-up: PGS001788 is the closest competitor (same paper family, same endpoint, very large validation n, but materially lower PRS-comparable R2=0.0163). Among the UKB sparse snpnet COPD variants, PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334 are direct COPD matches with explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 reported, but they are from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework and show weak PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC ~0.54; PGS-only R2 ~0.002–0.003), making them less supported than the global-biobank PRS-CS-auto COPD models despite their cleaner PRS-only AUROC reporting. (Non-exact endpoints like emphysema and chronic airway obstruction were deprioritized versus exact COPD endpoints.)

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034), both aligned to the target via trait_efo and with identical phenotyping_reported/trait_reported (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”), same publication family (UKB portability framework), same training cohort (UKB), same covariates, same validation sample size, and essentially identical reported partial correlation (0.0562 vs 0.0563). With no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and no effect sizes, performance evidence is limited and does not clearly separate them. Given the domain guidance fallback when PRS-only AUC is absent, the main differentiator becomes structural/method signals; PGS002034 uses LDpred2 with far more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is a modestly supportive structural advantage over a sparse penalized regression score in this context. Confidence remains low and the overall outcome is sub-optimal because both candidates come from a portability framework study and lack stronger, PRS-comparable performance reporting to justify a high-quality direct recommendation.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both report trait/phenotype as corneal dystrophy). All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (coronary artery disease / coronary heart disease mapped to CAD EFO), so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity plus the strongest PRS-relevant performance evidence without heavy risk-wrapper packaging. Confidence is not High because several near-clone siblings from the same publication family (PGS003726, PGS003727) have very similar endpoint/covariate framing and also strong HRs, and many other CAD scores report full-model AUROC values that are not PRS-comparable; thus, the ranking relies primarily on endpoint coherence + method/structure + effect-size evidence rather than directly comparable PRS-only metrics.

All 3 candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS004254 is preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto; 744,682 variants) and reports strong effect-size evidence (OR=2.18, 95% CI 2.05–2.32) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), which is supportive of meaningful PRS signal. The runners-up (PGS001331, then PGS001330) come from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-model framework ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as typically less externally robust; they do provide explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.58; PGS-only R2 ~0.006–0.007) and basic covariates, with PGS001331 slightly stronger than PGS001330 on these metrics. Overall confidence is moderate because the top choice lacks PRS-only AUC/R2 while the alternatives have PRS-only metrics but are framework-derived and one is time-to-event.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (dementia) are present, including multiple models with trait_efo=dementia and/or phenotyping_reported explicitly referencing incident all-cause dementia. PGS005170 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity to the target (phenotyping_reported: incident all-cause dementia; trait_reported: all-cause dementia; trait_efo: dementia), uses an integrative multi-PRS construction (explicitly combining 24 component PRSs; very large variant count), and reports a PRS-relevant effect size (HR=1.25) plus an AUROC (0.761) in the selected European validation context. Key limitation: the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 shown), so cross-model comparability is imperfect and lowers confidence.

Runners-up were ranked by remaining direct-match support emphasizing phenotype alignment and usable performance evidence while discounting pan-trait/framework origins: (1) PGS000823 has strong dementia endpoint fidelity (incident all-cause dementia) and a large evaluation sample (n=12,978) with a reported HR contrast (top vs bottom tertile) though lacks PRS-only metrics; (2) PGS001775 has an incident dementia endpoint with very large validation (n=458,181) and a strong HR (high vs low quintile), but includes many non-genetic covariates which makes reported performance less PRS-comparable; (3) PGS004281 is an all-cause dementia model with a reported AUROC (~0.819) using only basic covariates, but it is a single-record UKB-based method paper and provides no PRS-only metrics; (4) PGS000812 directly targets incident dementia with a per-SD HR estimate but has smaller validation (n=2,052) and weaker effect size than the higher-ranked dementia-endpoint alternatives. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.
